summary.text:
US equities dropped as investors pivoted to defensive assets and tech retreated, pressured by Nvidia falling 5.47% to 168.89 after Alibaba announced plans to list rival chipmaker T-Head. The S&P 500 slipped 0.38% to 7520.9302 and the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.6%, whereas European equities advanced, with the CAC gaining 0.55% to 8278.5898.

The dollar index firmed 0.12% to 102.355, pushing the euro down 0.58% to 1.1157 and sterling down 0.82% to 1.3331. In commodities, gold rose 0.91% to 4066.7, while Brent crude gained 0.75% to 92.18 and WTI added 0.41% to 86.39. Bitcoin traded slightly higher at 73927.0078, up 0.28%.

Key factors to watch include upcoming Big Tech rules from Brussels, updates on Anthropic targeting a $1.5tn IPO valuation, and corporate advertising trends after ITV warned of a 5% to 10% revenue decline in the fourth quarter.
